topic: Resuscitation and physical health equipment on psychiatric wards

audits.title: A closed loop two cycle audit investigating the availability and accessibility of physical healthcare equipment on forensic inpatient wards within mersey care's secure division
audits.standard: Care Quality Commission 2019 'Brief Guide: Physical Healthcare In Mental Health Settings' recommended equipment
audits.setting: Forensic inpatient wards (low, medium, high and secure learning disability), Mersey Care secure division, with non-secure wards as control

cycle1.result: Mean equipment availability 66% (range 50.9%-88.9%) across secure division; 75% (range 61.1%-88.9%) on non-secure control wards

audits.intervention: Findings presented and physical health equipment boxes placed in ward clinic rooms

cycle2.result: Mean availability 73.5% (range 72.2%-77.8%); mean percentage increase 12.5% (range -12.5% to 41.8%)

audits.other_findings: Gloves, pulse oximeters, sphygmomanometers, thermometers and stethoscopes became available on all wards, but availability remained below non-secure wards; further intervention and re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Davies T, Owens S, Forjoe T. A closed loop two cycle audit investigating the availability and accessibility of physical healthcare equipment on forensic inpatient wards within mersey care's secure division. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S74-S74.

audits.title: Availability and Functionality of Physical Health and Resuscitation Equipment in an Inpatient Setting: A Closed Loop Audit Cycle
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists 'Physical Health in Mental Health' and Resuscitation Council UK mental health inpatient equipment and drug lists, in line with trust standards
audits.setting: Four acute adult inpatient wards, mental health hospital, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 90.0% of standards met; physical health equipment available and functional 83.8%; resuscitation equipment 94.2%

audits.intervention: Awareness presentations at clinical governance meetings, complete equipment sets on each ward, registration on the maintenance database, engineering maintenance, and weekly (previously monthly) resuscitation equipment checks

cycle2.result: 90.0% of standards met (144/160 items in stock and functional); physical health equipment 76.6% (49/64); resuscitation equipment 99.2% (95/96)

audits.other_findings: Physical health equipment availability fell; a named staff member, a physical health equipment checklist and an electronic checking platform (My Kit Check) were proposed.
audits.citation: Tang S, Fadlalla I. Availability and Functionality of Physical Health and Resuscitation Equipment in an Inpatient Setting: A Closed Loop Audit Cycle. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S178-S179.

audits.title: Audit of Resuscitation Equipment in a Mental Health Setting – Resulting in Trust-Wide Action
audits.standard: Local Trust policy and Resuscitation Council UK standards for resuscitation equipment and weekly checklists

cycle1.result: 7/10 locations did not meet standards (missing or expired adrenaline, suction, oxygen masks); 4/10 wards had not completed the weekly checklist; 70% of staff-completed checklists were incorrect.

audits.intervention: Updated, more detailed checklist, standardised procedure for ward managers, regular audits and extra Resuscitation team staffing.
audits.other_findings: A re-audit was done and changes are being rolled out Trust-wide, but re-audit results are not reported.
audits.citation: Knowles N, Husain N. Audit of Resuscitation Equipment in a Mental Health Setting – Resulting in Trust-Wide Action. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S243-S243. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.591.

audits.title: Closing the Gap: Ensuring Minimum Required Physical Health Equipment Is Available on Inpatient Wards: An Audit
audits.standard: RCPsych Physical Health in Mental Health (2009) equipment checklist; compliance standard 100%
audits.setting: Seven inpatient wards (acute adult, older adult, forensic), The Redwoods Centre, Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: All wards >80% compliant; overall compliance 87%; neurological testing pins absent on most wards; alcometers, Snellen charts, ophthalmoscopes and otoscopes borrowed between wards.

audits.intervention: Formal equipment-sharing arrangements confirmed and procurement of missing equipment planned
audits.other_findings: Re-audit planned 6 months after the first cycle.
audits.citation: Obaid H, Capraro M, Evans H, Maumi G. Closing the Gap: Ensuring Minimum Required Physical Health Equipment Is Available on Inpatient Wards: An Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S327-S327. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11805.

audits.title: The physical healthcare of patients in secure hospitals: setting standards for medical equipment
audits.standard: Locally created audit standard for physical health equipment
audits.setting: Five clinical areas, medium secure forensic unit, Southern Health NHS Foundation Trust
audits.intervention: Redistribution and reorganisation of equipment, then ordering further equipment and separating daily from specialist equipment.
audits.citation: Hood A, Andersson J, Jones C, Gardiner L. The physical healthcare of patients in secure hospitals: setting standards for medical equipment. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S193-S194.
